question.problem:
Given that $g(x,y,z)=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1)}{z}$ and

$$
\frac{∂g}{∂x}=\frac{2x}{z({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1)},\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}=\frac{2y}{z({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1)},\,\frac{∂g}{∂z}=-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1)}{{z}^{2}},
$$

find the set of values $(x,y,z)$ where all partial derivatives of $g$ exist.
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that $g(x,y,z)=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1)}{z}$ is defined only when ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1>0$ and $z\ne 0.$ So, the domain of $g$ is 

$$
{D}_{g}=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}>1,\,z\ne 0\}.
$$

As for the partial derivatives, we have the following.

- The function ${g}_{x}(x,y,z)=\frac{2x}{z({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1)}$ is defined only when ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1\ne 0$ and $z\ne 0.$ So, the domain of ${g}_{x}$ is 

$$
{D}_{{g}_{x}}=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\ne 1,\,z\ne 0\}.
$$

- Similarly, the domain of ${g}_{y}(x,y,z)$ is the same: 

$$
{D}_{{g}_{y}}={D}_{{g}_{x}}=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\ne 1,\,z\ne 0\}.
$$

- The function ${g}_{z}(x,y,z)=-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1)}{{z}^{2}}$ is defined only when ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1>0$ and $z\ne 0.$ So, the domain of ${g}_{z}$ is 

$$
{D}_{{g}_{z}}=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}>1,\,z\ne 0\}.
$$

Finally, we conclude that the partials of $g$ exist on the set

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{g}\cap {D}_{{g}_{x}}\cap {D}_{{g}_{y}}\cap {D}_{{g}_{z}} & ={D}_{g}\cap {D}_{{g}_{x}}\cap {D}_{{g}_{z}} \\  & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}>1,\,z\ne 0\} \\  & \,\,\cap \{(x,y,z)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\ne 1,\,z\ne 0\} \\  & \,\,\cap \{(x,y,z)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}>1,\,z\ne 0\} \\  & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}>1,\,z\ne 0\}\end{aligned}
$$
